query_text: Create a serialized fiction reader voting app where fans of ongoing stories can vote on which direction the next chapter should go, with a reading area on one side and a voting panel on the other, all running in a desktop web browser so it feels like a proper community gathering place.

Build a magazine photo archive community site where people can browse old magazine spreads, add captions to photos, and tag who or what is in each image, with a clean browsable library on one side and a tagging area on the other, all for desktop browsers so it's easy to work through a lot of images at once.

A community recommendation app for people who want to study science journalism, where members can share articles, recommend sources, and leave notes on what made a piece good or where the research came from, running as a web app so you can explore it properly on a desktop with everything laid out side by side.

Make a film criticism aggregator app for desktop browsers where movie fans can write long reviews together, link to each other's takes, and see all the reviews for a single film collected in one place, with a sidebar listing films and the main area showing the full conversation of reviews.

Make a podcast transcript editor tool that runs in the browser so I can paste in a rough auto-generated transcript, clean it up paragraph by paragraph, and then publish it as a readable web page — I just want to stop copying and pasting between five different apps every time a new episode drops.

Make a newsletter analytics tracker for desktop browsers where I can see how many people opened each issue, which links got clicked, and how the subscriber count is changing over time, all in one place so I stop digging through three different tools just to figure out if anyone actually read what I sent.

Need a story pitch tracker web app where our editorial team can log every pitch that comes in, mark it as under review, accepted, or passed, and leave notes on why so we stop losing track of good ideas buried in a shared inbox.

Need a paywall and subscriber conversion tracker for our web app where I can see how many free readers hit the paywall each day, how many of them actually signed up, and which articles are converting the most — I just want one place to watch whether the paywall is actually doing anything instead of guessing.

A browser-based push notification composer tool for news publishers where you can write a short breaking news alert, preview exactly how it will look on different devices, and send it out with one click — because right now writing and sending these takes way too many steps across too many tabs.

Build a press credential application portal as a web app where journalists can fill out their info, upload their ID and past work samples, and track the status of their application, and where the organizer side can review and approve or reject each one without having to chase people over email.

Create a UNESCO world heritage site portal website that feels grand and reverent, like flipping through a beautifully printed atlas — rich full-width photos for each site, a warm earthy color palette, and a browsable map so you can wander through heritage sites by region the way you'd explore a well-made coffee table book.

Create a literary foundation and writers house website that has the quiet, unhurried feeling of a well-loved independent bookshop — warm cream tones, generous white space, author portraits that feel intimate rather than promotional, and a clean calendar of readings and residencies for desktop browsers where you can actually linger.

A national film archive and cinematheque showcase app for the web that feels like stepping into a beautiful old cinema lobby — moody dark tones, vintage film poster aesthetics, a browsable catalogue of classic films organized by era, and a screening schedule section that makes you actually want to show up, all designed for desktop browsers.

A natural history museum specimen and diorama gallery app for desktop browsers that feels like wandering through the hushed, wonder-filled halls of a great museum — deep forest greens and aged wood tones, large specimen photos you can zoom into, and collections organized by taxonomy so curious visitors can follow their own trail of discovery.

Create a botanic garden plant collections website that feels alive and a little wild — lush photography, soft sage and moss greens, an ecology section that tells the stories of ecosystems rather than just listing species names, all laid out beautifully for desktop browsers so it feels like a slow Sunday morning in the garden.

Build a public art installation and sculpture trail guide app for desktop browsers where the whole thing feels like a curated gallery walk — each artwork gets its own atmospheric photo and story, there's a map you can follow to plan a trail, and the overall vibe is editorial and considered rather than touristy.

An online museum collection browser app for desktop browsers where the home screen feels like a beautifully lit gallery — artworks displayed generously with room to breathe, filterable by period or medium, and each piece opens into a full story about its history and the artist, with that same quiet reverence you feel standing in front of a real painting.

Create a human rights case documentation portal website that feels serious and trustworthy — clean stark typography, a structured way to browse cases by country or theme, and a reporting area where each case gets its own carefully laid-out record so the gravity of the content is matched by the care of the design, built for desktop browsers.

A government audit and transparency report library app for desktop browsers where the whole thing feels like a well-organized reading room — reports grouped by year and department, a search that actually works, and each report presented cleanly so a curious citizen can sit down and actually read through the thing without fighting the interface.

Need a literary foundation author essay and spotlight hub that works as a beautiful web app for desktop browsers — the kind of place where an author's photo, biography, and a curated set of their essays all live together in one thoughtfully designed space, with the reading area feeling calm and literary, like an independent magazine you actually want to read slowly.

Create an archaeological excavation findings publication website that feels like a cross between a field journal and a museum exhibit — earthy tones, maps of dig sites alongside photos of what was uncovered, and each finding written up with the kind of careful storytelling that makes you feel like you were there, all designed for desktop browsers.

A public health awareness educational content center app for desktop browsers that feels warm and approachable rather than clinical — soft, friendly colors, illustrated guides organized by health topic, and a reading experience that makes complicated health information feel genuinely accessible to anyone who lands on the page.

Build a film festival audience award voting app for desktop browsers that has real personality — the kind of site that feels like it belongs to a festival with taste and history, where visitors can browse the competing films, cast their vote for their favorite, and see sponsor spotlights woven in naturally rather than slapped on as afterthoughts.

A heritage preservation sponsorship site for the web where donors and sponsors feel like they're genuinely part of something worth caring about — each monument gets its own story and photography, the sponsorship tiers are presented with dignity rather than desperation, and the whole thing has the kind of quiet gravitas that makes you want to reach for your wallet.

Need a public library capital campaign fundraising site that actually has soul — the kind of website that makes you feel the community love behind it, with a live fundraising goal tracker, donor wall, and impact stories that show what the money actually builds, all for desktop browsers and with a warmth that feels like the library itself.

Environmental pledge campaign site for a nonprofit coalition — a web app that carries real weight and intention, the kind where visitors actually feel the mission the moment the page loads, with a place to sign the pledge front and center and a live count showing how many people have already committed, so the whole thing feels like something that matters and not just another form.

Food bank hunger awareness month donation drive app — a website that feels genuinely urgent and warm at the same time, for desktop browsers, where the whole front of the app leads with why hunger month matters, has a clear donation amount selector with an impact line that says something like "feeds a family for three days", and a running total so visitors can see the campaign building in real time.

Create a web app for an animal shelter adoption drive campaign that actually feels alive and full of heart — the kind of site that leads with real success stories from pets who found homes, has a dedicated section where people can browse animals currently up for adoption, and carries the identity of a shelter that genuinely cares, for desktop browsers so the stories can breathe with some proper layout.

Make a vendor booth reservation app for a cultural festival so organizers stop juggling emails back and forth — a web app where vendors can browse available booth spots on a simple layout, pick their dates, fill in their info, and submit a reservation request all in one go, and organizers can see all pending bookings in a list on their side.

Need a registration app for art workshops and masterclasses that just works — a browser-based tool where people can see all upcoming sessions in a list, click one to get the details, and sign up without having to email anyone or hunt for a form, and where the organizer can see who's registered for each class.

Need a booking app for museum corporate events and private hire so clients can just handle it themselves — a web app where companies can see available dates and spaces, submit their event requirements and guest count, and get a confirmation, so the museum staff isn't stuck taking phone calls and writing everything down by hand.

Create a web app for paying public library fines and topping up your account balance so people can just do it online instead of going in person — a simple browser-based tool where you log in, see any outstanding fines with what they're for, pay them with a card, and also add credit to your account for future holds or prints, all on one straightforward page.

Build a web app for buying charity gift cards and e-vouchers where the whole flow is quick and painless — you pick a cause you care about, choose a gift card amount, pay, and get a digital voucher you can send to someone or redeem yourself, so giving to a charity feels as easy as buying anything else online, for desktop browsers.

Need a marketplace app for licensing cultural heritage IP for merchandise — a website where brand owners can list the heritage designs or characters available for licensing, and businesses can browse what's available, see the usage terms and pricing, and submit a licensing inquiry, so both sides can find each other and get the paperwork started without a middleman making phone calls.

Make a booking app for heritage building conservation tours so people can finally reserve their spot online instead of calling — a web app where visitors can see which buildings are on the tour schedule, check available dates and times, pick a slot, and confirm their reservation, so the organizers have all the bookings in one place and don't have to take notes over the phone.

Create a booking app for school groups to visit a science museum — a web app where teachers can log in, see available visit dates and time slots, enter how many students and chaperones are coming, and submit a booking request, so no one has to send an email and wait three days for someone to confirm they got it, for desktop browsers.

Build a volunteer shift sign-up app for a food bank so coordinators stop manually tracking who's coming in on what day — a web app where volunteers can see the weekly schedule, pick an open shift, put their name down, and get a confirmation, and where staff can see at a glance how many people are signed up for each slot.

Create a booking app for community legal aid consultations so people can schedule a session without having to call during office hours — a web app where you can see what types of legal help are available, pick an open time slot with one of the advisors, enter a brief description of your situation, and confirm your appointment, for desktop browsers.

Build a scheduling app for animal shelter meet-and-greet appointments so people who want to adopt a pet can book time with a specific animal — a web app where you browse the animals that are available for meet-and-greets, pick a date and time, leave your contact info, and get a confirmation so the shelter staff knows you're coming and which pet to have ready.

Make a session booking app for a nonprofit grief counseling service so people can schedule a counseling appointment on their own time — a web app where someone can see the available counselors and their open slots, pick a time that works, briefly describe what kind of support they're looking for, and book the session, all through a simple browser-based tool.

Need a learning app for environmental stewardship education aimed at nonprofits — a web app that has a list of lessons or modules on topics like conservation, sustainable practices, and community action, lets users track which lessons they've completed, and includes a short quiz or reflection at the end of each one so people actually retain what they learned, for desktop browsers.

Create a study and annotation app for primary source documents — a web app for desktop browsers where you can load a historical document, read it side by side with your own notes, highlight specific passages, and tag each highlight with a category like "evidence" or "context" so everything stays organized and you can actually review your annotations later in one tidy list.

Build a web app for collecting and studying community oral histories — a place where people can submit their own recorded stories or written accounts, and where visitors can browse the collection filtered by neighborhood or decade, listen to or read each story, and leave a comment or connection note, so the whole thing functions as a living archive that grows over time, for desktop browsers.

A legal rights and civic literacy learning app for desktop browsers — the kind of web app that organizes topics like voting rights, tenant protections, and government structure into clear sections, lets you work through each topic at your own pace, and includes a short self-check at the end so you know what you actually understood, with a sidebar that shows your progress through the whole curriculum.

A museum virtual exhibition app for desktop browsers that works like a proper guided learning experience — you move through the exhibit room by room, each stop has an artifact or image with a write-up, there's a short question to think about before moving on, and at the end you get a summary of what you explored so you can look back at the highlights without starting over.

Build a web app for exploring neighborhood history and local heritage — a learning tool for desktop browsers that lets you browse stories and photos organized by street or era, save the ones you find interesting to a personal list, and see a simple timeline of key moments in the neighborhood's past, so you can go deep on one area or just wander through the whole history.

Make a web app for organizing supporters around a grassroots civic campaign — something where volunteers can sign up to help, see what tasks need doing like phone banking or flyering, claim a task they want to take on, and post a quick update when they're done, so the campaign organizer has a live sense of who's doing what without chasing people over text.

Build a web app for participatory budgeting where community members can submit spending proposals and vote on each other's ideas — a browser-based tool where anyone can write up a project idea, explain what it would cost and who it helps, and the rest of the community can browse all the proposals and cast their votes, with a running tally showing which ideas have the most support.

Need a web app for a neighborhood council to post meeting agendas and minutes and collect feedback from residents — a browser-based tool where the council can upload notes from each meeting, residents can read through them, and anyone can leave a comment or reaction on specific agenda items, so there's an actual record of what was discussed and what people think about it.

A public comment and civic dialogue app for desktop browsers where residents can weigh in on local issues — the kind of web app where a city or community group posts a topic they want feedback on, people can read what others have already said and add their own comment, and there's a simple way to see which topics are getting the most discussion so nothing important just disappears into a long thread.
